subject: Revere Beach Historical Overview
overview: Host Laura Duggan interviewed historian Lou Spagnola regarding the development of Revere Beach as the first public beach in America. The discussion covered its 19th-century origins, legendary amusements, and the impacts of urban renewal and environmental events.

items.title: Introduction and Guest Background
items.summary: Host Laura Duggan introduced Lou Spagnola, a Medford Vocational High School teacher and Revere Beach historian.

items.title: Sarah Bradley Fulton Statue Dedication
items.summary: Duggan announced the dedication of the Sarah Bradley Fulton statue at Medford City Hall on April 20th.

items.title: Origins of Historical Interest
items.summary: Spagnola described how his research into digital newspaper archives in 2017 led to his expertise in Revere’s history.

items.title: Charles Elliott and the Public Beach Vision
items.summary: The discussion detailed Charles Elliott’s 1890s vision to create an open public beach by clearing shoreline buildings through eminent domain.

items.title: Town Naming and Revolutionary War History
items.summary: The participants reviewed the naming of the town after Paul Revere in 1871 and the significance of the Battle of Chelsea Creek.

items.title: Historic Preservation and Lost Landmarks
items.summary: Spagnola and Duggan discussed the loss of historic houses to development and the successful preservation of the Chevalier Theatre.

items.title: Revere Beach Amusements and Roller Coasters
items.summary: Spagnola recounted the history of famous attractions such as the Cyclone, the Lightning, and various beachfront fun houses.

items.title: Shoreline Railroad History
items.summary: The guest explained the 1875 construction of the narrow-gauge railroad and its eventual relocation to accommodate the public beach sweep.

items.title: Archival Photo Presentation
items.summary: Spagnola presented a series of historical images showing the Great Ocean Pier, the original bathhouses, and beachfront hotels.

items.title: Urban Renewal and the Blizzard of 1978
items.summary: The discussion addressed the decline of the amusement district following state land acquisitions and the impact of the 1978 blizzard.

items.title: Food Culture and Social Traditions
items.summary: The guest highlighted iconic concessions like Kelly’s Roast Beef and the history of summer-long dance marathons.

items.title: Wonderland and Regional Tourism
items.summary: Spagnola provided a timeline for Wonderland Amusement Park and discussed how commercial air travel impacted local beach tourism.

items.title: Teaching and Musical Career
items.summary: Spagnola shared details about his teaching style at Medford Vocational and his side career as a professional bass player.
